Title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles: SeoulS
Article:
Seoul, Sept 12, 2026 (AFP) -
North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles Saturday, Seoul said, a day after South Korea concluded five days of joint maritime drills with the United States and Japan that were focused on the North.
Pyongyang last month slammed plans for the so-called Freedom Edge joint exercises in international waters off South Korea as a "threat" to North Korea and other countries of the region.
On Saturday, Seoul's military detected "multiple short-range ballistic missiles launched from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea," also known as Sea of Japan, the Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a statement.
The missiles were detected at around 05:20 am (2020 GMT Friday) and flew around 250 kilometres (155 miles), they added.
South Korean and US intelligence authorities "have tracked and shared relevant developments since the initial stage of the launch and also shared information regarding the ... missile with Japan," the JCS statement said.
In its last test, North Korea fired a barrage of missiles into the sea on August 20, despite an overture from US President Donald Trump, who said he planned to meet this year with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
That launch from the nuclear-armed North came as South Korea and the United States held a shorter edition of their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercises, following an order from Trump to scale them back.
Trump's order alarmed US allies in the region, with the president calling the drills "inappropriate and hostile" towards North Korea.
But Seoul's spy agency told lawmakers earlier this month that a summit between the US and North Korea appeared possible "at any time" as signs have emerged of dialogue between them.
Trump met Kim three times during his first term – once declaring they were "in love" – in high-profile summits aimed at securing a denuclearisation deal, but no tangible progress was made.
- 'An evident disaster'  -
Pyongyang has long condemned US-South Korea joint exercises as rehearsals for invasion, often staging missile launches around the drills.
Trump, seeking to revive the bond he claims to have forged with Kim in his first term, told reporters at the White House on August 19 he plans to meet the North Korean leader this year.
The US president also said it was important to "get along" with Kim, adding that Pyongyang now had 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons.
Hours after the August 20 missile launches, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of the North Korean leader, said Trump's decision to scale back the drills with South Korea was Seoul's punishment.
She called it in a statement "an evident disaster brought by the unrealistic and anachronistic security outlook" pursued by Seoul, arguing the South had a "master-and-servant" relationship with the United States.

Title: Man arrested over alleged murder of mother in Tambunan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Police arrested a 31-year-old man on suspicion of murdering his mother at a rented house in Kampung Katagayan, Tambunan, yesterday.
Keningau district police chief superintendent Erwansyah Abdul Basir said police were alerted to the incident involving the 56-year-old victim at about 2pm and subsequently tracked down the suspect.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim died at the scene from injuries believed to have been inflicted with a sharp weapon.
"Villagers apprehended the suspect at a hut in Kampung Sutung, Tambunan, before handing him over to police.
"The suspect was taken to the Tambunan police station, where he was arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department team from the Keningau district police headquarters," he said in a statement today.
Erwansyah said the investigation team and forensic personnel had inspected the scene and seized several items believed to be linked to the case.
He said the victim's body had been sent to the hospital for a post-mortem examination and the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
"The public is urged not to speculate or spread unverified information about the case," he said.

Title: Magnitude 6.6 earthquake strikes Indonesia's Java region
Article:
HAMILTON: A 6.6 magnitude earthquake struck near Teluknaga in Indonesia's Northeastern Java province on Friday, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing the US Geological Survey (USGS).
The earthquake occurred at 4.23am local time (2123 GMT) on Friday at a depth of approximately 358.6km (222.8 miles).
There were no immediate reports of casualties or significant damage.

Title: 'Mount Kinabalu trespassers should face jail'
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: People who violate Mount Kinabalu should be jailed to deter others from desecrating the sacred park in Kundasang, Ranau, deputy state secretary Datuk Jamili Nais said.
"Climbing the 4,095m mountain by encroaching on the trail network should be deemed a criminal act."
Jamili, who once served as Sabah Parks director and was a custodian of the revered mountain, said this following the recent rescue of a 46-year-old Croatian climber in a five-day operation involving dozens of personnel from various agencies.
The climber, Mauro Persic, who less than a fortnight ago took part in an extreme adventure race in the Tambatuan area of Kota Belud, ascended Mount Kinabalu via an eastern route, a trail that links to villages that depend on spring water sources in the Kundasang area.
"Climbing the sacred Mount Kinabalu without a valid permit and through an unauthorised route ought to be criminalised. Violators should spend time in jail to deter others," he said.
He said eastern Europeans had been caught committing similar violations before, using excuses such as being unaware of the regulations or not understanding the language.
"I know for a fact this is not the first time, nor will it be the last."
Trespassers would also likely defecate along the unauthorised routes they use, spoiling the natural surroundings in their wrongful quest, he said.
"Their actions defile an area considered a sacred place by the Kadazandusun, Murut and Rungus communities, including those living around the foothills of the mountain.
"When something goes wrong, they cause a lot of inconvenience and waste a lot of money in search and rescue efforts," Jamili added.
Persic sent a
distress signal
last weekend, triggering a rescue effort involving the Fire and Rescue Department, Sabah Parks, mountain guides, porters, medical personnel and police.
Persic appeared to have fallen and sustained injuries. Rescuers found him and, by Thursday night, brought him from about 3,000m to Timpohon Gate, the starting point of the Mount Kinabalu trail. He was then sent to the district hospital, where he is recuperating.
Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the whole episode serves as an important reminder to all climbers to use only official routes, engage licensed operators and strictly follow the instructions of mountain guides.
Kota Kinabalu Native Court judge Rocky Mabin said that, in addition to criminal charges that could be brought against those who violate park regulations, Native Laws could also be used to prosecute trespassers.
"Trespassers are considered disrespectful of a sacred resting place for the departed.
"This is according to the old ways of our community," Rocky said, stressing that Mount Kinabalu must be respected.
The community believes that bad things can happen if the mountain is disrespected, citing the June 5, 2015 earthquake as an example.
Seven foreign tourists had posed nude along the summit trail shortly before the earthquake. Some were eventually reprimanded and deported.

Title: Stronger Asean health cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia on Thursday opened the 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, with Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad chairing the gathering for the first time in 22 years under the theme "Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems".
Dzulkefly, who chaired the meeting as Malaysia holds the Asean Health Ministers' chairmanship, with Myanmar as vice-chair, said the gathering marked a new phase in regional health cooperation, focusing on translating policy into action for Asean's 670 million people.
"The chain of survival is only as strong as its weakest link. Strengthening every stage is vital to securing a resilient and healthy region," he said in his opening address at the meeting here on Thursday.
The five-day conference, which began on Monday and ended yesterday, brought together health ministers and senior health officials from Asean member states, along with dialogue partners, World Health Organisation (WHO) representatives and technical experts.
BLUEPRINT FOR NEXT 5 YEARS
The centrepiece of this year's meeting was the launch of the Asean Strategic Health Agenda 2026-2030, a five-year roadmap for regional health cooperation across four core clusters.
It covers promoting healthy lifestyles and preventing non-communicable diseases, responding to all hazards and emerging public health threats, strengthening health systems and access to care and ensuring regional food safety.
Dzulkefly said the blueprint aimed to narrow health development gaps so that no Asean community or country was left behind, in line
with the broader Asean Community Vision 2045.
Malaysia's chairmanship also prioritised pandemic preparedness, with the meeting expected to strengthen the operationalisation of the Asean Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases, as well as developing an integrated strategy to address the dual burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases in the region.
BILATERAL MILESTONES
On the sidelines of the AHMM, Malaysia held bilateral engagements with key partners during the ministerial-level sessions.
With Singapore, both sides reaffirmed a memorandum of understanding on health cooperation, expanding collaboration in digital health, active ageing and regulatory reliance between Malaysia's Medical Device Authority and Singapore's Health Sciences Authority.
The arrangement, which took effect in March, aims to accelerate access to innovative medical devices in both countries.
With Indonesia, discussions covered digital health, traditional and complementary medicine and cross-border healthcare.
Malaysia's role as a medical tourism hub was also highlighted, with the country recording more than RM2.2 billion in medical tourism revenue last year.
Dzulkefly said he looked forward to equally strategic bilateral sessions with dialogue partners China and Japan to expand technical cooperation and investment ties in healthcare.
REGIONAL BREAKTHROUGHS
Several milestones were recorded during technical sessions preceding the ministerial-level meetings.
Malaysia chaired the inaugural Asean Roundtable Discussion on Medical Devices, where member states agreed in principle to support a phased Single Submission Model for pre-market approval, with Malaysia serving as the coordinating entry point for technical dossiers.
The model is expected to streamline medical device regulatory processes across the region and reduce time-to-market for medical innovations.
The meeting also saw the launch of the Asean Action Plan for Lung Health.
Malaysia shared its experience with artificial intelligence-assisted chest X-ray screening and proposed that Asean adopt a unified regional position to elevate lung health as a fundamental human right, in view of the growing burden of respiratory diseases.
A combined technical side event, convened under the leadership of Health Ministry director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab, covered eye health through the MySPECS initiative, neglected disease research under the Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative and behavioural insights.
Malaysia also used the occasion to advance work on rare diseases, with the handover of Malaysia's Rare Diseases Playbook taking place in support of the World Health Organisation Global Action Plan on Rare Diseases.
DIPLOMATIC DEVELOPMENTS
The AHMM also featured the inaugural Asean-United States Health Ministers' Meeting and Asean-Japan Health Ministers' Meeting.
There were also meetings with China, South Korea and WHO, which was represented by the Western Pacific Regional Office.
Dzulkefly said the platforms reflected deeper regional engagement with major global powers on issues beyond bilateral concerns, including pandemic preparedness, antimicrobial resistance and the integrity of pharmaceutical supply chains.
COMMITMENT TO ACTION
In his closing remarks, Dzulkefly said Malaysia's chairmanship would be measured not by the ambition of its agenda, but by the quality of its implementation.
"Guided by the values of Malaysia Madani, we remain firmly committed to turning health policy into tangible action for the 670 million citizens of Asean — for a better and healthier Asean."
The Health Ministry said the initiatives and policy frameworks discussed at the AHMM reflected Malaysia's commitment under the Madani framework and the consensus of Asean member states to ensure public health services remained inclusive and sustainable.

Title: 30 bodies recovered from burned ferry, 54 still missing off western Philippines
Article:
MANILA: The Philippine Coast Guard said Friday that 30 bodies had been recovered from the charred remains of a passenger ferry that caught fire off the western Philippine province of Palawan earlier this week, while 54 people remained missing, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The MV June Aster was initially reported to be carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members when it departed Manila for Coron in Palawan before catching fire Wednesday night.
Five people were confirmed dead that same night, while 43 passengers and crew members were rescued.
The number of people possibly missing was revised from 86 to 84 after two individuals listed on the manifest confirmed they had not boarded the vessel.
The Philippine Coast Guard said in a statement that authorities reported an initial count of 30 bodies recovered aboard the vessel after the fire was extinguished and a safety assessment was completed. — BERNAMA

Title: Nod for Kolej Poly-Tech Mara's Diploma in Accounting
Article:
BANGI:  The recognition of Kolej Poly-Tech Mara Sdn Bhd's (KPTMSB) Diploma in Accounting (AA101) by the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants (MICPA) will strengthen  pathways towards professional accounting qualifications.
KPTMSB chief executive officer Radzuan Razali said the recognition reflected the programme's alignment with academic and professional standards set by MICPA.
He said it would expose students to professional accounting standards, practices and expectations beyond the lecture hall.
"An education programme's excellence is no longer measured solely by academic achievement, but also by graduate employability, professional competency, industry exposure, soft skills and curriculum relevance.
"Through this collaboration with MICPA, we want to ensure our students not only have accounting knowledge and skills, but also understand the standards, practices and expectations of the profession."
Radzuan said the Diploma in Accounting was among the college's key programmes, with about 1,900 students enrolled across its campuses.
He said the figure reflected strong interest in accounting  at the college, placing greater responsibility on the institution to ensure its graduates acquired skills relevant to the profession.
The recognition also provides a clearer pathway for graduates towards the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) (Malaysia) qualification, subject to MICPA's requirements.
"CPA may look like a simple abbreviation, but the journey towards it is not simple. With effort, discipline and proper guidance, something that may seem distant can become achievable," Radzuan  said.
He said KPTMSB and MICPA could explore broader collaboration in academic development, knowledge transfer, professional competency development and networking opportunities for students.
He said MICPA's expertise in corporate governance, taxation, assurance, financial reporting and accounting and auditing standards would complement the college's academic strengths.
The strategic collaboration and MICPA recognition ceremony for the Diploma in Accounting  was held at KPTM Bangi's Grand Hall  on Wednesday.
The ceremony also saw the formalisation of a strategic collaboration between KPTMSB (through KPTM Bangi) and MICPA.
Radzuan said the recognition was not an endpoint, but a foundation for deeper cooperation between the two organisations.
"KPTMSB intends to continue and expand its collaboration with MICPA, including efforts to obtain recognition for the Bachelor of Arts in Accounting and Finance (AA231), in collaboration with the Dublin Business School, in the future.
"This reflects our continued commitment to strengthening the quality of accounting education and providing wider academic and professional pathways for our students."
KPTMSB operates six college campuses and Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia, offering programmes in information technology, computer science, health sciences, social sciences, accounting, business management, engineering, humanities and bio-industry.
Since 1983, KPTMSB has expanded access to affordable higher education and developed opportunities for students to pursue further studies.

Title: US judge blocks Trump administration's 'loyalty' question for job applicants
Article:
BOSTON, (United States): A federal judge on Friday blocked US President Donald Trump's administration from continuing to ask applicants for civil service jobs throughout the government to respond to what unions described as a partisan "loyalty question."
US District Judge George O'Toole in Boston sided with three unions representing government workers who sued last year after the administration began asking applicants for nonpartisan federal jobs to write essays explaining how they would help advance Trump's policies and executive orders.
The unions, including the American Federation of Government Employees, argued the question mandated by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) unlawfully politicized the hiring process for career government workers by attempting to assess their support for the Republican president.
O'Toole, an appointee of Democratic President Bill Clinton, said the question had been asked of applicants to positions ranging from an air traffic control specialist to a crane operator to a nuclear materials courier.
He said the unions' members reasonably interpreted it as an attempt to determine the applicants' political views, even though the Civil Service Reform Act bars making employment decisions for such jobs on the basis of political affiliation.
"The plaintiffs are thus likely to succeed in showing that there is no legitimate governmental interest in inquiring into the political beliefs of applicants to federal civil service vacancies," O'Toole wrote.
The judge halted the use of the question on grounds that it likely violated the Administrative Procedure Act by infringing on speech rights under the US Constitution's First Amendment.
Lawyers for the unions at the liberal group Democracy Forward welcomed the ruling, saying that over 70,000 federal job postings had included the question, undermining what is supposed to be a merit-based hiring system.
"Requiring federal job applicants to answer politically motivated questions goes against the very nature of the nonpartisan civil service," AFGE National President Everett Kelley said in a statement.
The other two unions are the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees and the National Association of Government Employees.
OPM did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It has previously defended the question as optional and said that it had been clear that hiring decisions could not be based on political beliefs.
It had adopted the question in response to an executive order Trump signed in January 2025 that required it to develop a hiring plan that brought into the federal workforce "only highly skilled Americans dedicated to the furtherance of American ideals, values, and interests."
OPM in a May 2025 memo to the heads of all executive agencies set forth various actions to implement Trump's order, including by requiring that job applicants be asked to respond to the essay question.

Title: High-profile cases keep courts busy this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It was another busy week at the courts, with high-profile personalities and closely watched cases taking the limelight.
The courts were abuzz with a teenage murder trial, Interpol's assistance sought to locate former research officer Yusoff Rawther, former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim's court appearance, three more alleged gang members being charged with murder and a corporate chief executive claiming trial to cheating charges.
Yusoff's case took another turn after the prosecution sought Interpol's assistance in Manchester to locate him as it moves to personally serve an appeal notice seeking his presence at the Court of Appeal in relation to his acquittal, instead of having him participate in the proceedings online.
Yusoff's lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali said his client has been in the United Kingdom since June and is seeking asylum on human rights grounds.
The prosecution had appealed against the decision to acquit and discharge Yusoff without calling for his defence over charges of trafficking 305g of cannabis and possessing two imitation pistols.
Below are the other big cases this week:
THE Bandar Utama school murder trial entered its final stretch, with the prosecution and defence completing their oral clarification before Shah Alam High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid.
The judge fixed Sept 14 for the decision in the case involving a 15-year-old boy accused of murdering his 16-year-old schoolmate, who sustained more than 180 stab wounds.
AZEEZ, whose court appearance turned into a waiting game for the media as he was to face a charge under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act.
Journalists, photographers and videographers had gathered at the court lobby as early as 7am, only to learn that Azeez had already been brought into court through an internal route for remand proceedings for fraud probe under the Penal Code.
After almost eight hours, the media finally got their chance when Azeez emerged in a purple lock-up uniform and handcuffs at the underground-floor bail payment counter.
According to the charge, Azeez, who was then TH chairman, is alleged to have used his position to secure the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which came with annual remuneration of RM690,000, as well as the use of a BMW 7 Series and a full-time driver.
He was released on RM450,000 bail and later released from a two-day remand on Thursday evening.
ON Thursday, Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad, 67, claimed trial to two cheating charges involving shipping daily charter rates.
Azmi is accused of cheating Iskandar Mohd Zaffa, a principal officer at TH Alam Management Sdn Bhd, by concealing the actual daily charter-rate offers in two separate transactions and inducing him to agree to contracts carrying lower rates.
In the first charge, Azmi allegedly concealed an RM80,500 daily rate offered on Aug 24, 2023, and induced Iskandar to agree to a contract at RM70,000 per day.
In the second charge, he allegedly concealed an RM110,000 daily rate offered on Jan 15, 2024, and induced Iskandar to agree to a contract at RM78,000 per day.
Azmi was granted a RM300,000 with one surety bail.
IN Shah Alam, three more alleged gang members were charged in the magistrate's court with murdering a 23-year-old man during an illegal gathering at Taman Alam Megah last month.
The latest charges bring the total number of individuals charged in connection with the case to 11, after eight men were charged with the same offence last week.
Police said a fight broke out among a group of men believed to be gang members before a car struck the victim, killing him on the spot.
The incident went viral after a dashcam recording of the incident was circulated online.
In the one-minute recording, several men were seen rushing out of vehicles and attacking a man lying on the road.
Another car was then seen making a U-turn and striking the victim, before several others continued attacking him.

Title: Saudi says drones launched from Iraq hit oil pipeline
Article:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia on Friday said drones launched from Iraq hit the East-West pipeline and led to its closure.
The foreign ministry condemned "the targeting of the East-West pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions by several drones coming from Iraq, which caused human injuries and damage".
"The pipeline was stopped as a precaution, and the attacks resulted in some injuries," an energy ministry official told the SPA news agency earlier.
"At the request of the Iraqi prime minister... (Riyadh) has chosen not to respond at this stage and to support the efforts of the Iraqi government ... to prevent attacks launched from Iraq against the Kingdom and neighbouring countries," the foreign ministry said.
But it stressed that Saudi Arabia "reserves the right to take all necessary measures to protect its sovereignty, its security, its facilities," and its inhabitants.
Saudi Arabia says the attacks that occurred on Thursday morning had left several people wounded.
Since the start of the war in the Middle East, Riyadh has increased its use of this pipeline, which links Abqaiq, near the Gulf, to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, in order to bypass the closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran. — AFP

Title: Drug lab, slain syndicate chief, airport security gaps and Nibong Tebal abduction among major crimes this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have shut down a large-scale drug processing laboratory hidden inside an industrial premises in Selangor, seizing more than 13 tonnes of liquid and powdered MDMA and other drugs estimated to be worth RM2.4 billion in Op Eumenes.
The operation followed intelligence and surveillance on the syndicate, with six simultaneous and follow-up raids conducted in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur where it saw five suspects aged 29 to 43 arrested.
The haul comprised about 7.09 tonnes of liquid MDMA and 6.06 tonnes of MDMA powder, alongside 1.04kg of cannabis, 880g of Erimin 5 pills, 180g of ketamine, 150g of yaba pills and 50g of methamphetamine.
The syndicate, believed active since February, sourced precursor chemicals and drug-processing machinery from China before bringing them into Malaysia.
The industrial premises were used for processing and storage, with various machines and equipment also seized during the raids.
Police also seized five vehicles and other assets worth RM276,000 under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988.
Below are some of the major crimes reported in the country this week.
THE man shot dead by police during an anti-drug operation in Seremban on Sept 6 is believed to have been the mastermind behind a clandestine laboratory in Bandar Puncak Alam capable of producing drugs worth an estimated RM2.4 billion.
Investigations showed the 52-year-old man headed the syndicate, overseeing the recruitment of members and bringing drug-processing equipment into Malaysia from overseas.
Investigations revealed the syndicate sourced precursor chemicals and equipment believed to have originated from China, falsely declaring them as processing equipment before importing them through Port Klang.
Police believe a Taiwanese national arrested in the earlier operation acted as the syndicate's chemist, while several members remain at large.
Investigations were ongoing into possible links to Taiwan and overseas markets, including Indonesia.
GAPS in airport security screening have come under scrutiny after a Malaysian woman was detained at Indira Gandhi International Airport in India with more than 15kg of ganja worth about RM2.24 million, after arriving from Kuala Lumpur.
Delhi Customs said the woman arrived at Terminal 3 before being identified through passenger profiling.
An inspection of her trolley bag uncovered 30 plastic packages containing a substance suspected to be ganja, which was subsequently seized under India's Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.
Malaysian police believed the 22-year-old woman was a drug mule. Police records also showed she had a previous drug-related case.
IN Penang, five people have been remanded for four days to assist investigations into the abduction of a 52-year-old man whose body was found inside a septic tank at a house in Taman Seri Bistari, Nibong Tebal earlier this week.
The suspects, aged between 25 and 35, comprise three Malaysians, including the house owner, and two Myanmar nationals.
Police arrested the five suspects at several locations in the Seberang Prai Selatan district in separate operations.
The arrests followed investigations into the man's abduction and subsequent discovery of his body which was found at the rear of a single-storey terrace house, with his hands and legs bound.
Police believe the body had been inside the septic tank for about two days before it was discovered.

Title: Anwar, Putin move to fast-track bilateral deals, improve direct air connectivity
Article:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Russian President Vladimir Putin have agreed to fast-track the implementation of bilateral agreements while pushing ahead with measures to strengthen air connectivity between the two countries.
A key outcome of their meeting on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit here was Putin's agreement to establish a special mechanism to expedite the execution of bilateral agreements, aimed at translating government commitments into tangible economic outcomes.
The two leaders also discussed expediting direct air connectivity between Malaysia and Russia, alongside visa-free travel, which could facilitate greater movement of tourists, business travellers and investors between the two markets.
Anwar also raised the prospect of increased Russian imports of Malaysian palm oil, potentially opening wider market access for Malaysian producers and strengthening agricultural trade between the two countries.
He also expressed appreciation for Russia's support for energy cooperation with Malaysia, highlighting the sector's potential to become a stronger pillar of bilateral economic relations.
The proposed special mechanism would provide a more structured channel for both governments to monitor and accelerate the implementation of agreements across key sectors, reducing delays between commitments and actual execution.
During the meeting, Anwar conveyed the regards of Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, and reiterated the ruler's invitation for Putin to undertake a state visit to Malaysia.
The discussions underscore Malaysia's push to move beyond diplomatic engagement and deliver more concrete commercial outcomes with Russia, while leveraging its BRICS partnership to expand trade and investment links with major emerging markets.

Title: Umno, Pas tie-up a win-win for both parties, say analysts [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional could gain more, both electorally and politically, by forging a partnership with Pas rather than by working with Pakatan Harapan, said political analysts.
Dr Lau Zhe Wei said BN would have better prospects of winning more seats and securing the top leadership position through cooperation with Pas.
"If BN were to work with Pas, the outcome would likely be better for them compared with  working with PH."
Lau was commenting on Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's remarks in his policy speech at the Umno General Assembly that BN could undergo an "evolution" if it forged a strategic partnership with another political force, particularly when "blue" meets "green".
Without naming any party or political coalition, Zahid, who is also BN chairman, said such a development could occur when the two forces come together.
Lau said the current political landscape and the strength of Malay unity sentiments made Pas a more suitable partner for BN than PH.
He pointed to developments in Johor and Negri Sembilan as indications of the current political dynamics.
He said a partnership with Pas could not only improve BN's electoral prospects, but also give it greater political leverage to secure the country's top leadership position.
[[nid:1530924]]
"Working with Pas,  not only can  they (BN)  win more seats, but  Pas is also willing to give the highest leadership to BN.
"If BN were to work with PH, could they still  pick   the prime minister? Most likely not."
He said one of the key issues that would need to be resolved in any BN-Pas cooperation was the leadership arrangement.
"One of the small issues  arising  is in Melaka, where the question is whether the arrangement should be led by  Pas or BN."
Lau said reaching a consensus in Melaka, as well as in Pahang and Perak, could help resolve potential differences and prevent similar issues from emerging at the federal level.
"I would say that if BN wants to find a partner, it would   definitely be Pas rather than PH. BN would   only choose to go on its own and contest independently if it cannot strike a deal with Pas."
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said cooperation between BN and Pas could be beneficial, as it would allow the parties to consolidate Malay votes rather than split them.
"The victory may appear easy, but for a general election, for example, it could still be quite difficult. Although they can combine their votes, can both parties divide the seats fairly?"
Mazlan said this was the  main challenge facing the two parties.
[[nid:1530923]]
"If they can reach a fair seat-sharing arrangement, then there would be no issue."
He  also said Zahid's remarks reflected a stronger interest within Umno to cooperate with Pas, particularly as relations with PH appeared to be deteriorating.
He said this was  evident following several issues, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission investigation into Tabung Haji and Felda, as well as controversies involving Zahid's ministry.
"In previous statements, we saw that Umno did not seem particularly serious about Pas.
"But lately, it seems like they have become very close. It appears that Umno is now taking more initiative in moving forward with Pas."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ebola infections top 7,000 in Congo as virus spreads to new province
Article:
DAKAR: The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 7,000, with the virus spreading to a new province, government data showed on Friday.
The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, became the largest and deadliest in Congo's history after surpassing the 2018–2020 epidemic.
It is now second only to the 2014–2016 West African outbreak, which infected over 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000 across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.
Government figures showed late on Friday that the death toll had risen to 3,398, while confirmed cases reached 7,022 across seven provinces.
Officials told Reuters earlier on Friday an Ebola case had been detected in South Ubangi province, located in the northwest of the country, far from the epicentre of the outbreak.
Shortages of trained staff, operational partners and funding are causing a bottleneck in efforts to expand the Ebola response, according to the World Health Organization. — REUTERS

Title: Train derails in northwest France, 44 injured
Article:
PARIS: A train carrying 186 passengers derailed in northwest France on Friday, injuring 44 people, one of them seriously, officials said.
The train was running between the Normandy cities of Rouen and Caen, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said on X.
It derailed around 7.45pm (1745 GMT), local authorities said in a statement, and a mass-casualty response plan had been activated, with 130 firefighters, five medical teams and 80 vehicles deployed.
"Suddenly there were a few jolts, and then after about three seconds it got stronger and stronger," one of the passengers, Louis, 24, told ICI Normandie radio.
"I couldn't stay in my seat any more," he said. "The windows partially shattered, the stones from the track came into the carriage. It was really shocking. I'm still shaking."
Rouen prosecutor Sebastien Gallois said 44 people were injured including an 18-year-old woman evacuated "in a critical condition", while tests for drugs and alcohol on the train driver had come back negative.
SNCF Reseau, which controls the French rail network, told AFP that traffic on the line has been suspended and power to the tracks cut to allow emergency services to operate.
"The priority is to care for the passengers and then to restore safe operating conditions," SNCF Reseau said.
Rail authorities and the police are investigating the causes of the accident. — AFP

Title: North Korea launches unidentified projectile, South Korea says
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea launched an unidentified projectile toward the sea to the east of the Korean Peninsula, South Korea's defence ministry said on Saturday.
South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported earlier that South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff are analysing the projectile's specifications and range.
Last month, North Korea launched more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles and ordered its military to maintain full readiness during South Korea's ongoing joint exercises with the US.
Saturday's launch came a day after South Korea, Japan and the US concluded their joint military drills to test readiness against North Korea's missile and nuclear weapons threats.
Separately last month, US President Donald Trump abruptly scaled back military drills, which he described as hostile to Pyongyang, and said he expected to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un later this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran says to discuss Hormuz with Gulf states in Oman on Monday
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry said the country would meet with Gulf states in Oman on Monday to discuss the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which the Islamic republic has blockaded during the Middle East war.
"This meeting is intended to promote better understanding among the countries of the region and help strengthen shared regional security," the ministry said in a statement on Friday.
"Iraq and other littoral Persian Gulf states" will participate, it added.
Iran has been at war since February 28, when US-Israeli strikes killed its supreme leader.
Iran retaliated with attacks across the region and blockaded the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed.
More than six months into the Middle East war, the blockade continues to drive up oil prices, which soared past $100 a barrel this week.
Oman and Iran, which both border the Strait of Hormuz, have been discussing for several weeks how the crucial waterway will be managed in the future.
The strait was free to transit before the war, but Iran now requires vessels to obtain permission and is considering a mechanism to impose service fees.
Ships that do not comply are regularly targeted by Iranian strikes, while the United States periodically bombs the Iranian coastline to challenge the Islamic republic's control of the strait.

Title: Remember the 5 heroes who delivered hope to interior Sarawak
Article:
AS we celebrate Malaysia Day next week, we are reminded that sometimes, it takes a tragedy to pull us together as Malaysians.
When a friend related earlier this week   how he cried over an amateur video of an apparently stricken helicopter on a Flying Doctor Service run deep in Sarawak's interior before it hit the ground and was incinerated, I knew this incident will cut deeply.
Five Malaysian heroes, all in their prime, paid with their own lives while extending otherwise hard-to-access, life-saving medical services to isolated native communities in Borneo's jungle-clad highlands.
The routine services provided by the likes of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, her assistant Alexson Adit Henry and staff nurses Debra Moset and Jessie Paya Jok (age 44, the oldest in the group) and pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham would otherwise be largely unheralded had their mission not gone so horribly wrong.
Tributes came thick and fast, from the king and prime minister down to ordinary netizens on social media.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg promptly announced a state payout of RM100,000 to each of the five families, as well as to the Sarawak Foundation for picking up the tab for the education of all their schoolgoing children.
It did not matter if the five who perished were from Kelantan or Negri Sembilan or Sarawak. They were all Malaysians serving fellow Malaysians and having their lives cut short in the process.
The tragedy brings into sharp relief the often difficult and unforgiving terrain some Malaysians in rural Sarawak still live in.
Were it not for the Flying Doctor Service,  they would have to endure trekking on foot — sometimes for days — to reach the nearest medical clinic.
Family obligations mean that some children from these communities sometimes have to choose between getting an education in a boarding school in the nearest town or quitting altogether to assist parents with farm work.
It will be impractical and exorbitantly costly for the government to build and staff clinics and schools to serve these far-flung communities. Thus, programmes like the Flying Doctor Service  will be here to stay, despite the latest mishap.
As with the Rural Air Services, which the government continues to subsidise to the tune of a couple hundred million ringgit annually so that isolated communities in Sarawak and Sabah have a decent link to the outside world, there is probably no viable alternative to the Flying Doctor Service  in the foreseeable future.
The government will have to search deeply for whatever shortcomings resulted in this tragic accident, review the operations of the Flying Doctor Service  and adhere to recommendations once official investigations are complete.
Malaysians take many things for granted. Among them, that almost free healthcare is accessible to almost all of us, including those among us living in the
most inaccessible parts of the country.
On Malaysia Day this year, we must count our many blessings as Malaysians even as we mourn the five heroes who died while delivering one of the most vital blessings in some of the most remote places of the country.
The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Finally, AI governance
Article:
MALAYSIA'S first ever dedicated horizontal legal framework on artificial intelligence (AI) governance is ready to be tabled in Parliament in Q1 2027.
All must welcome the Bill. But Parliament must ensure that the law is strong enough to protect the public without being so rigid that it stifles innovation.
The move is timely, but AI cannot wait for perfect laws. AI is already being used in business, education, healthcare, finance, government and everyday life.
Malaysians are also increasingly exposed to AI-generated scams, impersonation, deepfakes and misinformation.
A clear legal framework can provide certainty for businesses and protection for the public. The Bill should be seen not as an attempt to slow AI, but a way to build trust in its use.
Not all applications pose the same danger. Low-risk uses should not face the same excessive regulatory burdens. Stricter requirements should apply to high-risk or high-impact AI, especially in healthcare; finance and credit decisions; employment and recruitment; education; policing and public safety; critical infrastructure and public services.
There are reasons aplenty for such a cautious approach, the most practical of which is AI risk management. The United Kingdom, Singapore, Canada, Japan, South Korea and a few other countries — all started with businesses, education and simply commercial arrangements between and among themselves.
Singapore, our closest neighbour, didn't begin its AI with one single invention. Like most nations around the globe, it was a slow process.
First came AI capabilities through computerisation, through universities, government research and national strategies and plans.
There will be those who are enthusiasts and those who are  lukewarm in their support driven by the "unknowns". These are the ones who stand in between two extreme ends of the spectrum, the other extreme end being the so-called "protesters".
Singapore's interest in computing isn't recent either. As usual, it was the government which did the legwork. In 1963, the Central Provident Fund, Malaysia's EPF if you like, automated its administrative work which in turn pushed the Singapore civil service into more robust computerisation.
Then came the National Computerisation Plan, Computerisation Masterplan followed by research by the Island State's top universities.
That is in short  Singapore's early computerisation story. Today, the story has been refreshed.
This year, Singapore has established the National AI Council, placing artificial intelligence as a central part of the city-state's technology strategy.
Malaysia must ensure that there is human accountability in all this. Machines for humans, not humans for machines.
AI should assist people, not an excuse for organisations to avoid responsibility. Where an AI system makes or significantly influences a decision a person makes about a job, a loan, healthcare or rights, there should be meaningful human oversight.
Someone must be ultimately accountable when AI causes harm. The law must give Malaysians the right to know when AI is involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'That's why we fight': Trump links 9/11 to Iran conflict
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump vowed Friday that the United States would never forget the Sept 11, 2001 attacks and suggested the country was continuing the "war on terror" 25 years later by fighting Iran.
Speaking at the Pentagon after skipping the main 9/11 commemorations in New York, Republican Trump also hit out at domestic "fanatics" in an apparent swipe at Democrats.
"Today we renew the sacred oath that we first swore in their names a quarter of a century ago. We will never, ever forget. That's why we fight today," Trump said in a speech.
"We don't have a choice. There can only be victory. We fight hard. We fight to win," added the president, who was accompanied by First Lady Melania Trump.
One of the jets hijacked on 9/11 hit the Pentagon in Washington, killing 184 people who were remembered by a single bell tolling as their names were read out.
But presidents have previously marked major anniversaries by attending several sites including New York, where the majority of the 2,977 victims were killed in the attacks on the World Trade Center.
Trump went on to link the fight against Al-Qaeda launched by his Republican predecessor George W. Bush to the US-Israeli war on Iran which is now in its seventh month.
"Today we salute every member of the United States military who served in the 'War on Terror.' It is a war on sick, horrible terror," Trump said.
"And we salute the service members working right now to ensure the world's number one sponsor of terror, the Islamic Republic of Iran, will never ever have a nuclear weapon."
'ISLAMIC THEOCRACY'
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth also lashed out at Iran in his remarks to the Pentagon ceremony.
"Over the past six months, we have laid waste to the world's most prolific state sponsor of terrorism. Our warriors have fought an Islamic theocracy that has wished us death for nearly half a century," Hegseth said.
The Iran war has slid into a stalemate with Iran largely maintaining its grip on the Strait of Hormuz, and keeping oil prices high, despite sporadic exchanges of fire with the United States.
Trump also turned to the domestic front, a day after a Republican convention for the US midterm elections in which Trump and Vice President JD Vance accused Democrats of sympathising with the 9/11 attackers.
"A generation after 9/11, we also know that the final response to those atrocities and the ultimate victory over the perpetrators will not be found on a foreign battlefield," Trump said.
Telling the story of a firefighter killed in the attacks whose son went on to become a US Navy veteran, Trump said it showed that "we can be a nation whose heroes are not fanatics for an abstract cause."
In his speech to the Republican convention on Wednesday, Trump had used the same term: "With your vote in this election, you can tell these far-left lunatics and fanatics that America is not for sale to them or to anybody else."
Republicans at the convention repeatedly trained their fire on left-wing Democratic senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed over his previous social media posts about 9/11.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China's robot champion races towards real-world work
Article:
A WEEK after his robot outran humanity's fastest man, Jack Guo is already chasing a harder goal.
TianGong Ultra stunned spectators at the World Humanoid Robot Games when it covered 100m in 8.64 seconds, almost a full second faster than Usain Bolt's world record.
Behind the feat were days of round-the-clock testing and repairing battered robots between races.
"When it started smoothly and got past 50m, that was when I finally relaxed," said Guo, who leads the development of Ultra and Omni —  a smaller model used in 400m races —  at the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Centre, known as X-Humanoid.
A week later, the bespectacled 34-year-old engineer is already focused on a bigger challenge.
"We want to turn high performance into high reliability and high usability," he said in  his first interview with foreign media.
The record-breaking run offers a rare window into China's growing lead in humanoid robotics, where state-backed research, deep supply chains and intense competition are accelerating advances in machine mobility.
Yet Guo's next goal underscores a harder task facing the industry as it struggles to turn dazzling demonstrations into useful workers.
X-Humanoid sits in Yizhuang, a high-tech development zone in Beijing's southeast and one of China's main robotics clusters.
Long home to automakers, the district now boasts a robot sales centre and even a robot-themed restaurant, part of a push to showcase the industry.
The first-floor showroom traces generations of TianGong robots, including one that still wears the vest from a  half-marathon  win  last year.
On the ninth floor, white Ultra and Omni humanoids stand suspended in metal frames. One wears a red "Champion TianGong" headband.
In the adjoining office, Guo's team develops software before testing it on physical machines.
Established in November 2023, X-Humanoid is backed by state-owned and private investors along with domestic tech giants Xiaomi and Baidu. It develops hardware, motion-control software and artificial intelligence (AI) for the wider industry while commercialising its own robots.
X-Humanoid customers include universities, research institutes and companies exploring industrial applications.
At Foton Cummins' engine factory in Beijing, the company's robots have been trialled moving boxes, with its Tianyi 2.0 robot lifting 8kg to 12kg boxes onto shelves in what the factory described as an early-stage exploration.
Ultra was not originally designed to win a race. It started as an experiment to push the boundaries of humanoid movement.
Guo likens today's humanoids to the earliest cars: first make them controllable, then pair reliable bodies with smarter AI "brains" capable of handling complex tasks on their own.
Making a robot run develops generalised mobility, improving its ability to cope with different terrain.
The smaller Omni has already shown what that can mean in practice. In a test this year, it climbed from the first floor to the 17th floor of X-Humanoid's headquarters.
Guo expects smaller humanoids to find early roles in commercial services and light industry, while Ultra could eventually perform outdoor inspections or emergency rescues.
Ultra arrived at the Games armed with three running strategies trained in simulation. One was battle-tested, two faster on paper but less proven.
Each strategy is a trained motion-control system that continuously adjusts joints and balance, allowing the robot to sprint upright without an operator directing every step.
Ultra used a different programme in each race, running 9.39 seconds in the preliminary, 8.86 in the semifinal and 8.64 in the final.
Even on the morning of the final, the team was testing a newly trained running programme. It worked repeatedly during trials, but not on the competition track.
Differences between individual robots also created headaches, leaving Guo uneasy before the race.
Ultra's heavier legs limited early acceleration, but once it passed about 10m per second, it could keep building speed and reel in rivals. The team had shaved roughly half a second from its starting response by the semifinal, Guo estimated. From there, attention shifted to outright speed.
In the final, a faster reaction time and late acceleration allowed Ultra to pull off a more decisive overtake.
Backstage, the team celebrated. At the closing ceremony, a row of TianGong humanoids donned red capes emblazoned with "Champion", some waving pom-poms.
"Finally, I could get a good night's sleep," Guo said.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hong Kong sentences Tiananmen activists to between 5 and 7 years in jail
Article:
HONG KONG: A Hong Kong court handed three Tiananmen vigil activists jail sentences of between five and seven years on Friday for national security crimes, drawing international condemnation.
Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, Albert Ho, 74, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, have been behind bars since they were charged in 2021. Their sentences are expected to include time already served.
The United Nations, rights groups and foreign governments have condemned the sentences, issued under a national security law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020 following huge pro-democracy protests.
A court ruled in August that the activists had breached the Chinese constitution by calling for an "end to one-party dictatorship."
Lee and Chow, who pleaded not guilty, were sentenced to seven years and seven years and three months, respectively, AFP journalists in court heard.
Ho, a former lawmaker who pleaded guilty in January, got five years and two months.
The verdict held that although the case did not involve violence and the defendants had not put forward a specific timetable to carry out an "end to one-party dictatorship", their offence was still of "a serious nature."
Chow, a barrister who represented herself, told a hearing last month that she had "nothing to repent for."
She raised both arms and waved at supporters as she was escorted out by officers.
Supporters outside court hugged her mother, Medina Chow Lau Wah-chun, who said her daughter had maintained high spirits during the trial.
"She is not a competent barrister. She is simply an outstanding defendant," her mother said.
Lee crossed himself, smiled and bowed at his wife Elizabeth Tang Yin-ngor and supporters, including high-profile activist Cardinal Joseph Zen, who gripped each other's hands after leaving the courtroom.
"I'm really sad, and very angry," Tang told reporters, saying Lee would "definitely appeal."
Dozens of police swarmed around the court and set up cordons to hold back crowds.
'STERN WARNING'
Hong Kong and Macau were the only places on Chinese soil that permitted public mourning for those killed on June 4, 1989, when Beijing sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform around the capital's Tiananmen Square.
But public commemoration has been effectively banned in the cities in recent years.
The trio were leaders of the now-defunct Hong Kong Alliance, the group that organised annual vigils in the city's Victoria Park.
City leader John Lee said in a statement that "the law will never allow anyone to use the pretext of human rights, democracy and freedom to blatantly harm their own country and compatriots."
National security police chief Steve Li told reporters the sentences are "a stern warning to those who may be contemplating similar acts."
Taiwan, which China sees as its own territory, condemned the sentences, while a European Union spokesperson said the ruling "undermines confidence in the rule of law and harms Hong Kong's reputation."
UN rights chief Volker Turk "calls for these sentences to be quashed", his office said in a statement.
Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, said the "harsh sentences" expose "the cruelty and insecurity of a government afraid of memory and the people."
Urania Chiu, a legal expert, told AFP that the heavy sentences are "not only (for) overt acts of activism or advocacy, but also acts of remembrance."
The national security law "is actively shaping what is and is not allowed to remain part of the official history", she said.
'PILLAR OF SHAME'
The Hong Kong Alliance group also operated a museum dedicated to the crackdown and held events, including a yearly washing of the "Pillar of Shame" – a statue to mourn victims.
The statue was removed from its long-time plinth at the University of Hong Kong in 2021, and other local universities followed suit with similar objects.
Prosecutors argued that evidence in the case, including the statue and archives from the Hong Kong Alliance's museum, should be confiscated.
Judge Alex Lee said on Friday the fate of the statue would be decided after a decision was made on its ownership.
The Danish artist behind "Pillar of Shame", Jens Galschiot, called the outcome of the trial and the statue's potential confiscation "outrageous."
The statue tells the story of Tiananmen, said Galschiot, who has for years sought to reclaim his work.
If destroyed, that would also "destroy the story that everybody should know", he told AFP.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Scammers forge KL DoE documents to cheat suppliers out of RM200,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DoE) has detected eight government procurement order scams abusing its name, resulting in losses exceeding RM200,000 for two suppliers.
Director Sharifah Zakiah Syed Sahab said the department first detected the scam on Sept 4, when a representative from a diving equipment supplier visited to verify government procurement documents.
"Before that, the department received several inquiries regarding procurement documents starting in mid-August.
"Last Tuesday, a supplier representative inquired about a souvenir order worth over RM100,000, supposedly placed by KL DoE for an upcoming programme," she said yesterday.
Checks revealed that the department never placed souvenir orders or booked programmes. Instead, orders were made using forged documents featuring abused officers' names, fake letterheads, and forged management signatures.
"Based on information from the suppliers, they transferred more than RM100,000 to certain parties as advance payment for the souvenirs. KL DoE has asked them to lodge police reports," she said.
Sharifah Zakiah added that KL DoE filed a police report last Wednesday denying officer involvement and reported the matter to the DoE Headquarters Finance Division.
Despite police reports, the department received further inquiries regarding fake procurement orders.
"Another supplier was scammed with losses exceeding RM100,000. The department has referred these cases to the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department," she said.
She advised suppliers and contractors to exercise caution and verify all government procurement documents before making financial commitments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry urged to strengthen transport safety after helicopter crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Joint Council of Presidents and Secretaries-General of the Health Ministry Workers Union (Mapsu) has urged the Health Ministry to strengthen safety standards for air, sea and river transport used in healthcare services following the recent Long Lellang helicopter crash in Sarawak.
Mapsu president Ajulahin Japin said the safety of healthcare workers must be given serious and preventive attention.
"Although the actual cause of the incident should be left to an official investigation, Mapsu believes that safety aspects in all forms of transportation used for delivering health services, especially in rural areas, must be given serious and preventive attention," he said in a statement yesterday.
He said healthcare operations in Sarawak, Sabah and the interior regions of Peninsular Malaysia rely heavily on air, sea and river transport.
He said the ministry must not focus solely on aviation safety, but also ensure that water transport complies with strict safety standards.
Ajulahin added that the experiences and feedback of healthcare workers in the field should be incorporated into safety protocols, as they have firsthand knowledge of the operational risks in remote areas.
On Tuesday, a BO-105
helicopter crashed
near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Miri, Sarawak, killing five people.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah and Sarawak challenges must be part of national journey, says PKR Youth chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The history and challenges faced by Sabah and Sarawak must be viewed as part of Malaysia's collective experience to elevate the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) into a national narrative.
PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said a true national narrative goes beyond asking Peninsular Malaysians to understand the demands of the two Borneo states.
He said it requires recognising their experiences as part of the country's shared journey.
"The history of Sabah and Sarawak is our history. Poverty in the interior of Sabah is not solely a problem for Sabahans, just as educational disadvantage in Sarawak cannot be viewed as an issue far removed from the life of a young person in Selangor, Kedah or Kelantan," he said in a Facebook post today.
Welcoming Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call to implement MA63 as a national narrative, Kamil said the move opens broader avenues to discuss the rights of Sabah and Sarawak while encouraging Malaysians to re-examine their understanding of the country's history and the meaning of Malaysia itself.
He noted that more than six decades after Malaysia's formation, national discourse remains heavily centred on the Peninsula, while issues concerning MA63, the status of Sabah and Sarawak, development demands, and relations with the federal government are often treated merely as regional matters.
"After all, the history of Malaysia's formation never cast Sabah and Sarawak merely as footnotes to a nation that was already fully formed," he said.
Kamil said that while significant progress has been made and various MA63 matters have been resolved or restored through negotiations, nation-building cannot be achieved solely through constitutional provisions or the division of powers.
He said it requires a sense of belonging, equal opportunity, respect for diversity, and the conviction that every child born in Tawau, Kapit, Kangar, or Kuala Lumpur has an equal stake in the nation's future.
Malaysia, he added, was born out of the courage to build a federation spanning seas and territories, bringing together diverse cultural, religious, and historical backgrounds willing to share a common future.
"This is the true meaning of a federation, and it is a concept that must be understood as we strive to make MA63 part of the national narrative," he said.
His comments follow Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's remarks after chairing the 2026 MA63 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) meeting in Kota Kinabalu, where he emphasised that implementing MA63 must form part of the national narrative rather than being viewed as an issue specific to Sabah and Sarawak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cameron Highlands hit by landslide and flash floods after heavy rain [WATCH]
Article:
CAMERON HIGHLANDS: A landslide along Section 1.4 of Jalan Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah, Tanah Rata, forced the temporary closure of the road to all motorists this afternoon.
The incident, reported at 4.50pm, prompted the closure to ensure public safety and facilitate earth-clearing works by the Public Works Department (PWD) and YP Maintenance.
District police chief Superintendent Azri Ramli said authorities were closely monitoring the clearing works and would reopen the road once it was deemed safe.
"The situation at the location is under control, with regular monitoring being carried out. The public is advised to avoid the road temporarily," he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, a flash flood was reported at 4.53pm at Taman Perumahan Golden Hill, Brinchang, affecting three houses and seven vehicles.
Azri confirmed that no casualties or injuries were reported.
"Police personnel were deployed to the scene for further action and monitoring.
"Upon arrival, the situation was found to be under control and the floodwaters had begun to recede. The Fire and Rescue Department and Civil Defence Force were also informed for safety and monitoring purposes," he said.
Police advised the public, particularly residents in high-risk areas, to remain vigilant amid changing weather conditions and comply with instructions from the authorities.
Information can be channelled to the Cameron Highlands district police headquarters operations room at 05-491 5999 or any nearby police station.

Title: Anwar takes subtle jab at Zahid with 'Guru', 'slay' references
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has taken a subtle jab at his deputy, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, echoing the "Guru" and "slay" references used by the Umno president in recent remarks.
Anwar used both terms while updating Malaysians on his diplomatic mission to India.
"Praise be to God, Guru has safely arrived in New Delhi, India, to carry the country's name onto the world stage at the 18th BRICS Summit."
"Pray that this diplomatic mission achieves its objectives. May the students learn from Guru how Madani Diplomacy is put into practice. Slayyy," he said in a Facebook post.
Earlier at the 2026 Umno General Assembly, Zahid had taken a swipe at a leader whom he claimed had refused to listen to the people's grievances and concerns.
Referring to the
unnamed individual
as "Guru", Zahid, in outlining the Blue Malaysia Agenda, highlighted the impact of economic policies on ordinary Malaysians.
He also urged youths to be confident in putting forward their ideas, using the phrases "slay" and "flex" in a social media post.
Zahid's use of "Guru", or teacher, echoed a leaked telephone conversation between Zahid and Anwar in April 2021, during which Zahid referred to Anwar as "Guru."
Anwar is in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Title: Super El Nino could bring 40°C temperatures to Malaysia by early 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia faces an extreme heatwave with temperatures potentially reaching 40 degrees Celsius between January and May next year due to an impending Super El Nino phenomenon.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the probability of the phenomenon occurring is approaching 100 per cent, based on climate models from international observation and research centres.
MetMalaysia said that historical meteorological records associate strong El Nino episodes with elevated temperatures, dry conditions, and severe haze risks.
Previous Super El Nino events in 1997/1998 and 2015/2016 recorded daily maximum temperatures far more extreme than usual.
Notable high records include 40.1 degrees Celsius at the Chuping Meteorological Station in Perlis on April 9, 1998, and 39.3 degrees Celsius at the Batu Embun Meteorological Station in Jerantut, Pahang, on April 10, 2016.
MetMalaysia estimates a 70 per cent probability that the intensity of the upcoming El Nino will exceed any episode recorded since 1950.
The northern and inland areas of the Peninsular, alongside the interior of Sabah and Sarawak, are expected to experience higher-than-average temperatures and an increased risk of heatwaves starting from the end of the Northeast Monsoon through May 2027.
Based on the latest projections, more meteorological stations in northern Peninsular Malaysia are likely to record temperatures reaching 40 degrees Celsius during the peak dry period.
MetMalaysia also warned of an increased risk of forest fires and haze due to the hotter and drier conditions.
"Risks of fires and air pollution could increase," MetMalaysia said.
The department added that prolonged high temperatures elevate the risk of heatwaves and pose health hazards, particularly for children, the elderly, and outdoor workers.
Reduced rainfall and extended dry spells may stress water resources, including catchments and dams, while impacting water-sensitive agricultural and industrial sectors.
The prolonged dry climate renders vegetation more flammable, escalating the risk of peatland and forest fires alongside local and transboundary haze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver who crashed into Kajang eatery fell asleep, say police
Article:
KAJANG: A lorry driver whose vehicle crashed into the front of an eatery in Jalan Batu 12, Cheras, yesterday was believed to have fallen asleep at the wheel, and was not driving under the influence of alcohol as alleged online.
Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the incident occurred at 6.30pm as the lorry was heading towards Cheras.
He said the 37-year-old driver is believed to have fallen asleep, causing him to lose control of the vehicle before crashing into the eatery's front structure.
"The lorry suffered minor front-end damage, while the eatery sustained damage to its business umbrella and kitchen equipment.
"No casualties or injuries were reported," Naazron said in a statement today.
He added that police detected a video clip of the incident circulating on social media at 12.30pm today.
The viral video showed the lorry moving along the road after the collision, with an accompanying post claiming the driver was drunk and refused to stop.
Naazron said the case is being investigated under Rule 10 of the Road Traffic Rules 1959 (LN 166/59).
Those with information can contact the investigating officer, Inspector Saifudin Saadun at 011-2111 9379 to assist in the investigation.
Naazron also advised road users to drive prudently, abide by traffic regulations, and exercise caution to prevent unwanted incidents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Body of unidentified man found along Sungai Langat
Article:
KAJANG: The unclothed body of an unidentified man was found on the banks of Sungai Langat near Section 5, Bandar Baru Bangi, yesterday afternoon.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report on the discovery at 6pm and dispatched a team to the scene.
He said initial checks found the body on the riverbank, before Fire and Rescue Department personnel helped retrieve it.
"Preliminary checks by the Forensic Unit found no visible injuries on the body to suggest foul play.
"The body was sent to the Serdang Hospital Forensic Unit for an autopsy, but the cause of death has yet to be determined pending laboratory analysis," he said in a statement today.
Naazron said the case had been classified as sudden death.
Those with information about the incident or whose family member is missing can contact investigating officer Inspector Sutri Patang at 018-942 7088.
Footage of the discovery had earlier gone viral on social media.
