Title: New school curriculum to introduce Sabah identity elements in Year One and Form One next year
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 12 — Elements reflecting Sabah’s identity will be incorporated into the new school curriculum for Year One and Form One students from the next academic session, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said.
She said the initiative was among the agreements reached on education at the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) meeting here this morning.
Fadhlina said Sabah Education, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk James Ratib had given his full support to the proposal.
“Among the matters discussed was how we can continue to support education in Sabah based on the agreements and terms under MA63.
“The Sabah identity elements will be introduced in the new Year One and Form One curriculum from next year,” she told reporters after attending the handover ceremony for the Sekolah Menengah Sains Sabah and Sekolah Kebangsaan Buit Hill projects here yesterday.
Fadhlina said incorporating elements of Sabah’s identity into the curriculum was important in strengthening ties among Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, which she described as a foundation of Malaysia’s strength.
She said the initiative would enable younger generations to understand, appreciate and respect Sabah’s rich cultural heritage while allowing it to be shared more widely through the national curriculum.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said the placement of new teachers and appointments of principals and headteachers in Sabah were in the final stages of being completed.
On dilapidated schools in Sabah, the minister said progress was encouraging, with some projects completed and others under construction or in the pre-implementation stage.
She said the ministry was continuing to closely monitor the projects with relevant agencies, including the Sabah Public Works Department (JKR), to ensure upgrading works proceeded smoothly.
In her speech earlier, Fadhlina said 245 dilapidated schools in Sabah had been fully rebuilt, while another 63 were under construction and the remainder were at various stages of implementation.
They are among 416 dilapidated schools in Sabah identified for complete replacement, she said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia-Russia ties in focus as PM Anwar, Putin meet at Brics summit
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit here, providing an opportunity for both leaders to strengthen Putrajaya and Moscow’s relations and exchange views on matters of mutual interest.
It marked Anwar’s first bilateral meeting upon his arrival here to participate in the summit in Malaysia’s capacity as a BRICS partner country since January 1, 2025.
The meeting underscored the importance of maintaining high-level engagement between the two countries, particularly as Malaysia seeks to deepen economic and strategic ties with major emerging economies.
Malaysia and Russia have maintained longstanding diplomatic relations since 1967, with cooperation spanning trade and investment, energy, education, tourism, defence and other areas.
Both countries have also expressed interest in expanding bilateral economic engagement and exploring new areas of collaboration.
The meeting also came as Malaysia continues to advocate for a more inclusive and balanced international order while strengthening its engagement with the Global South through platforms such as BRICS and other multilateral mechanisms.
Anwar’s bilateral meeting with Putin further reinforced the commitment of both countries to constructive dialogue, closer cooperation and stronger people-to-people ties, while contributing to Malaysia’s broader foreign policy and economic objectives.
In 2024, total Asean-Russia trade amounted to US$18.1 billion, while Russian foreign direct investment in Asean totalled RM367.90 million (US$92.97 million).
For Malaysia, Russia was the country’s ninth-largest trading partner among European nations in 2025, with total trade was valued at RM8.72 billion (US$2.04 billion).
Malaysia’s primary exports to Russia included electrical and electronic products, machinery, equipment and parts, and processed food, while principal imports consisted of petroleum products, minerals, chemicals and chemical-based products. — Bernama

Title: Anwar welcomes Western push to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed the joint statement issued on September 8 by the foreign ministers of 12 Western countries regarding measures against illegal Israeli settlements.
He said the steps represent an overdue shift in the approach of several Western governments and must now be matched by firm implementation.
“These governments should use their considerable diplomatic and economic leverage over Israel to press for an end to settlement expansion and forced displacement, accountability for the devastation inflicted on Gaza and unimpeded humanitarian access,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Anwar said he noted in particular that Britain, Canada and France would bring forward measures to ban trade in settlement goods, joining several European countries that have already taken this step.
“I also recognise the significance of the statement by British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to the House of Commons. The United Kingdom has now formally recognised the unlawfulness of the Israeli occupation as a whole.
“It has also acknowledged that ethnic cleansing of Palestinians is taking place in areas of the West Bank at the hands of what Mr Miliband rightly calls ‘settler terrorists’. These are significant acknowledgements, grounded in international law and in the realities confronting the Palestinian people,” he said.
Anwar called on the international community to move beyond statements towards concrete and binding measures that uphold international law, protect the rights of the Palestinian people and secure a just and lasting peace in the Middle East.
Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden and the UK confirm their intention to introduce national and or support European restrictions on trade in goods with settlements which are illegal under international law, or that they are actively considering these and other measures, in accordance with their national procedures. — Bernama

Title: MCMC probes claims Claude AI targeted Malaysian voters, but says issue outside its mandate
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining claims that Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence platform was used to operate a commercial election manipulation campaign targeting users in Malaysia.
MCMC said it took the US AI company’s latest report seriously but stressed that the activities described fell outside its functions and mandate.
“MCMC was not involved in any activities or dealings as described in the report,” it said in a statement today.
Anthropic reportedly said it had identified and removed an account linked to a network of about 1,000 fake accounts on X, a fake news website and several fabricated dossiers or intelligence files.
MCMC said it was seeking further information and clarification from the relevant parties to establish the facts and understand the context of the claims.
“Based on the information and evidence obtained, MCMC will determine the appropriate follow-up action within its jurisdiction, including working with the relevant authorities,” it said.
The commission added that protecting the public from online harm and maintaining a safe and trusted online environment remained central to its responsibilities. — Bernama

Title: Anwar to meet Modi, leading Indian companies on Brics summit sidelines today
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to have three bilateral meetings today on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here.
The day starts off with a bilateral meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, followed by one with Anwar’s Indian counterpart and summit host Narendra Modi.
His third bilateral meeting is with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to have a pull aside meeting with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.
This will be followed by one-on-one business meetings, including with Adani Group, which has positioned itself to be the market leader in its transport logistics and energy utility portfolio businesses focusing on large scale infrastructure development in India.
Also lined up are Segula Technologies India Pvt Ltd, a global engineering group; AWL Agri Business Ltd, one of India’s largest food and fast-moving consumer goods companies; and Motherson Group, a leading global design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly, and logistics specialist.
Later in the day, the Prime Minister will attend a gala dinner for leaders of BRICS member, partner and outreach countries at the Bharat Mandapan, the exhibition and convention centre where the summit will take place.
The summit, themed “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, will focus on strengthening resilience, economic cooperation as well as trade and investment reforms.
As a founding member of BRICS, India has previously held its chairship three times — in 2012, 2016 and 2021. India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1, 2026.
Malaysia’s participation in the BRICS Leaders’ Summit is in its capacity as a BRICS partner country since January 1, 2025. — Bernama

Title: KL DOE warns of fake procurement scams after two suppliers lose more than RM200,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DOE) has detected several attempts by irresponsible parties to commit fraud using the department’s name.
Its Director, Sharifah Zakiah Syed Sahab, said that as of today, eight such cases have been detected involving government procurement order scams, resulting in losses totalling more than RM200,000 for two suppliers.
She said her department first detected the scam on September 4, when a representative of a diving equipment supplier came to the department to verify the authenticity of government procurement documents.
“Prior to that, KL DOE also received several inquiries regarding these government procurement documents starting in mid-August, and last Tuesday (September 8) from a supplier company representative who also came to inquire about a souvenir order worth more than RM100,000 supposedly made by KL DOE for an upcoming programme,” she told Bernama, here today.
She noted that checks by her department revealed that the department had never made any souvenir orders or programme bookings. Instead, the orders were made using forged documents that abused officers’ names, alongside fake letterheads and management signatures.
“Based on the suppliers’ information, they claimed to have transferred more than RM100,000 to certain parties as an advance payment for the souvenirs, and KL DOE has asked the suppliers to make a police report regarding the scam,” she said.
Elaborating further, she added that KL DOE also lodged a police report last Wednesday denying the involvement of department officers in the incident, while reports were also made to the DOE Headquarters Finance Division.
However, she mentioned that yesterday and today, her department still received inquiries regarding the fake procurement orders.
“In fact, today there was a supplier who was scammed with losses exceeding RM100,000, and the department has subsequently referred these cases further to the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department,” she said.
Sharifah Zakiah also advised all suppliers and contractors to be cautious and verify the authenticity of any government procurement documents they received. — Bernama

Title: Fire Dept: Two men found dead in separate incidents in Penang drain and Perak river
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 11 — Two men were found dead in separate incidents in Penang and Perak today, one in a drain near a school here and the other in Sungai Perak.
The body of Ooi Chai Siang, 37, was found in a drain about 1.5 metres deep near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Hussein Onn in Taman Kelisa Emas here today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call from the police at 12.10pm requesting assistance to retrieve the body.
“A team from the Perai Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) proceeded to the location and, upon arrival, found a man in the drain. The operation commander then instructed firefighters wearing full personal protective equipment (PPE) to retrieve the body,” he said in a statement today.
He said the body was handed over to the police for further action and later sent to the hospital for a post-mortem to determine the actual cause of death.
In Ipoh, the body of a 38-year-old man feared drowned after jumping into Sungai Perak to retrieve his boat, which had drifted away from a fish cage yesterday, was found this afternoon.
Perak JBPM Operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the body was found at 2pm, about four kilometres from the spot where he had jumped at Batu 18, Kampung Kuchai, near Bota Kiri.
“The search operation resumed this morning, involving 30 personnel, including the K9 Unit and Water Rescue Team (PPDA), within a six-kilometre radius along the river.
“The victim’s body was subsequently found floating by the PPDA team and brought ashore before being handed over to the police for further action,” he said in a statement today.
Earlier, Sabarodzi said the incident occurred at about 5pm yesterday when the man jumped into Sungai Perak to retrieve his boat. His nephew had attempted to rescue him, but the effort was unsuccessful. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar heads to India for BRICS summit, bilateral talks with world leaders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — After concluding his working visit to Sabah today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, where he is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was scheduled to meet the Prime Minister of India, as well as the presidents of Russia, Iran and Kazakhstan and the Prime Minister of Ethiopia.
“My delegation and I have departed for New Delhi, India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.
“My itinerary in India also includes a visit to Keralam to meet the Grand Mufti of India to exchange views on community development, education and religious affairs,” he said.
After completing his diplomatic mission in India, Anwar will proceed to Malé, Maldives for an official visit at the invitation of President Dr Mohamed Muizzu.
“May everything go smoothly and may this visit bring tangible benefits to the people and the country. Insya-Allah,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Past is past, but Umno delegates want PAS to prove it can be different
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Beside one of the ministry booths at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Muhammad Awang stood with a friend and picked up a copy of
Utusan Malaysia
from a pile laid out for delegates as others milled around the Umno general assembly.
At 68, the Umno Kuala Krai division secretary has seen the party’s relationship with PAS shift from cooperation to rivalry and back again.
But as Umno now looks to forge a fresh understanding with its former political rival, Muhammad believes the past should not stand in the way of trying again.
“We have to put aside our respective egos. We have to be big-hearted,” he told Malay Mail on the sidelines of the assembly here.
Muhammad said any renewed cooperation between Umno and PAS would require both sides to make compromises, particularly over the allocation of seats in the next election.
“If it is Kelantan, we should give it to Umno. Elsewhere, we should also give seats to PAS. Let it be balanced,” he said.
PAS members attend the Umno Youth General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur yesterday. — Picture by Yusof Isa
His comments came as Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi called for greater political understanding between the country’s existing political coalitions in his speech at the assembly this morning.
Zahid revived his proposal for a “Grand Collaboration”, which he said was not about merging political parties but creating an understanding to avoid political clashes that could be damaging to all sides.
He described the political understanding as one based on prioritising common interests, respecting differences in ideology and identity, and practising tolerance and flexibility.
But he also stressed that political partners must not betray one another, warning against building an understanding during the day while plotting to bring down a partner at night.
For Muhammad, that warning is particularly relevant given Umno and PAS’ previous experience under Muafakat Nasional.
“Umno and PAS had Muafakat Nasional before, but it never reached the stage of being translated into an election. We did not have the chance to see it through.
“So we do not want to split for a second time. We have been separated several times and we do not want to be bitten by the same snake in the same hole,” he said.
Still, Muhammad said the previous breakdown should not prevent both parties from trying again.
He said both sides would need to put aside their egos and be willing to make concessions for the sake of Malay-Muslim unity.
For him, that meant accepting that neither side could expect to get everything it wanted, including when deciding which party should contest certain seats.
An Umno Kuala Lumpur delegate in his 60s, who declined to be named, similarly said PAS’ previous political decisions should be treated as a lesson rather than an obstacle to future cooperation.
“This is politics. We should do whatever can benefit Umno,” he said.
Delegates gather at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur for the 2026 Umno General Assembly on September 11, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Muhammad acknowledged that there had been what he described as many instances of betrayal, including PAS previously discussing Malay-Muslim unity with Umno before choosing to work with other political partners.
But he said he personally believed Umno and PAS should work together in the next general election.
“If we are divided, we are not strong. So I see this as a good step towards making the Malays and Muslims strong again,” he said.
Asked whether the past should now be left behind, he replied: “Yes, exactly. It is a lesson.”
He said he hoped the relationship now being built between Umno and PAS would not repeat the problems of their previous alliances.
The willingness to move on, however, does not appear to mean delegates have forgotten what happened before.
Selayang Umno Youth chief Shah Zanuriman Nuar Paras Khan, 40, speaks to Malay Mail on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
For Shah Zanuriman Nuar Paras Khan, 40, the Selayang Umno Youth chief, rebuilding trust would require both sides to be clear about what they expect from one another.
“To avoid being betrayed, there needs to be a spirit of camaraderie, loyalty, mutual understanding and clear boundaries,” he said.
Shah added that the same stability delegates were looking for within Umno could also be important if the party were to work with other political partners.
“There are all sorts of disputes between the other parties. Bersatu is falling apart, then there are cracks here and there, and they are constantly fighting.
“Umno, meanwhile, remains stable. So I think that is what makes the people see Umno as remaining stable and maintaining its own momentum. There are no internal fights, no Camp A or Camp B, nothing like that.
“So perhaps the people are looking for stability amid an uncertain economic situation, and they see Umno as more stable than the other parties,” he said.
That balance between forgiveness and caution was also reflected in Zahid’s speech, where his call for political understanding was accompanied by a warning that agreements must be honoured.
Delegates said past political betrayals should serve as lessons rather than prevent Umno and PAS from working together again. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
The Umno president said political cooperation should allow parties to preserve their own identities, stressing that “Umno remains Umno” and “Barisan Nasional remains Barisan Nasional”.
For delegates like Muhammad, that may be the basis on which a new relationship with PAS can be built: not by pretending the past did not happen, but by deciding it should not dictate what comes next.
After years of political shifts between the two parties, he said it was time to try again with a more carefully negotiated understanding.

Title: Economy minister: Sabah receives RM582m, highest allocation for small-scale projects nationwide since 2023
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — A total of RM1.52 billion has been allocated for 8,069 small-scale projects and People’s Facility Initiatives (IKR) nationwide since 2023, with Sabah receiving the largest share at RM582.29 million for 2,301 projects.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said RM175.24 million of the allocation for Sabah was channelled for the implementation of 985 IKR projects, and RM407.05 million was for 1,316 small-scale projects.
For this year alone, he said, Sabah received RM113.3 million to implement 481 IKR and small-scale projects, out of a total national allocation of RM323.8 million.
“Every application must undergo an evaluation process to ensure the project is feasible, taking into account factors such as suitability, status and site availability, before funds are channelled to the implementing agencies,” he said.
He told reporters this after visiting an IKR project to upgrade a wooden bridge to a semi-concrete structure in Kampung Kalansanan here today.
On the need for concrete bridges in water-based settlements, particularly in Sabah, Akmal Nasrullah said the Ministry of Economy was considering making the construction of such facilities a priority under the IKR programme next year.
He said the matter warranted attention as bridges served not only as pathways for residents but were also important for safety, particularly during emergencies such as fires.
“For next year, under the IKR programme, we can make these small bridges a key focus area. When the ministry receives applications from residents or Sabah, we will prioritise these small bridge projects,” he said.
On the project he visited, Akmal Nasrullah said it was valued at RM199,508 and implemented by Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK) under the IKR programme, and was completed on January 13.
He said the project involved upgrading a bridge measuring 200 feet (about 70 metres) in length and 1.8 metres in width to improve safety and facilitate the movement of residents. — Bernama

Title: GISBH fails in bid to challenge Kedah fatwa declaring teachings deviant
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Alor Setar High Court has dismissed an application by GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and its Chief Executive Officer, Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, for leave to initiate judicial review proceedings to challenge a state fatwa issued against them last year.
The fatwa, issued by the Kedah State Fatwa Committee on February 12 last year, ruled that the beliefs, teachings, tenets and practices of GISBH members and followers were deviant and contrary to Islamic teachings.
The committee also ruled that any Muslim who acted in contravention of the fatwa committed an offence under the Syariah Criminal Offences Enactment (Kedah Darul Aman) 2014 and was liable to legal action under the laws in force in Kedah.
Judge Evawani Farisyta Mohammad dismissed the application by GISBH and Nasiruddin after allowing the Attorney General’s objection to their application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings.
In the grounds of judgment dated September 7, which was uploaded on the judiciary’s website, the judge said the contents of the fatwa were based on Syariah law and therefore fell within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Syariah Court, meaning that the Civil Court had no jurisdiction to determine the matter.
“…this court, regarding the reliefs sought by the applicants (GISBH and Nasiruddin), is essentially being asked to review the content or substance of the fatwa and to quash it,” she said.
Judge Evawani also said the fatwa referred to individuals involved with GISBH rather than GISBH as a corporate entity.
She noted that the fatwa was issued pursuant to the prerogative powers of the Sultan of Kedah and was therefore a decision that was non-justiciable and could not be challenged through judicial review.
In their application for leave, GISBH and Nasiruddin had sought an order of certiorari to quash the decision made by the respondents through the issuance of the fatwa.
The applicants named the Kedah State Fatwa Committee, Kedah State Islamic Religious Council and Mufti of Kedah as respondents.
Nasiruddin and GISBH claimed that the fatwa had adversely affected their operations and reputation, as well as those of individuals associated with them, and had resulted in them being perceived as followers of deviant teachings.
The Attorney General objected to the application on the grounds that the fatwa was not subject to judicial review or adjudication, as it constituted an exercise of the Ruler’s prerogative powers. — Bernama

Title: Penang LRT works to close part of Jalan Magazine for 21 days from Sept 14
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 11 — Jalan Magazine here will be closed for 21 days from September 14 to facilitate road widening and utility relocation works for the LRT Mutiara Line project.
Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) said the closure would be in effect around the clock from 10pm on September 14 until 5am on October 5.
“The closure will involve the leftmost lane of Jalan Magazine in front of St. Giles Wembley Hotel heading towards KOMTAR, while the other lanes will remain open to traffic,” it said in a statement today.
It said a partial lane closure would also be implemented intermittently along Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah from 8am to 4pm daily from September 16 to December 15 to facilitate construction of the LRT Mutiara Line, including drainage and road widening works.
The closure will involve the leftmost lane between the Sunny Point Complex traffic light junction and the Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) field heading towards KOMTAR, as well as the rightmost lane in front of the USM field and Batu Uban Army Camp in both directions.
“Other lanes will remain open to traffic at all times. Road users are advised to exercise caution when passing through the area.
“Road signs and traffic cones will be placed, while flagmen will be deployed to help manage traffic flow and ensure the safety of road users at the affected routes,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Chief minister says Melaka election not far off, dissolution of DUN required by year‑end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, September 11 — As talks and speculation on the upcoming Melaka state election intensify, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the wait will be neither too long nor too soon.
Speaking to the press during the 2026 Umno General Assembly at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL), Rauf said that that Melaka must dissolve its state legislative assembly (DUN) by the end of December as its five year term is nearing completion.
“Our efforts have been underway for the past two years.
“We are now merely waiting for the final curtain to fall on this work so we can dissolve the assembly.
“We can’t delay the dissolution of the DUN because the date is inching closer,” Rauf said.
When asked about the possible candidates, Rauf is keeping their identity pretty close to his chest however revealed that they are not closing the door for cooperation with other political parties if the people wants it.
When asked about the possible candidates, Rauf kept their identity pretty close to his chest, but shared that they are not closing the door to cooperation with other political parties if the people want it.
“We will leave it to the people to decide who the best strategic partner is for the Melaka state government.
“I have made it clear that any talks with political parties wishing to join the Melaka democracy stage will only happen once the DUN is dissolved,” Rauf said.
He added that he and his team will continue to fight for the 21 seats in Melaka that they’ve won previously and will not be compromising them for others.
“To contest is the right of any party, but we cannot compromise on the 21 seats we currently hold,” he said.
Aside from that, commenting on Umno’s president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi keynote speech this morning, Rauf has nothing but praise for the head honcho.
He said that the speech outlined a clear direction for Umno in rebuilding its strength not just for the upcoming state election but also for the upcoming general election (GE16).
“GE16 will be the turning point for Umno to become a dominant force in the country’s politics once again,” he said.

Title: Malaysians scamming Malaysians: Indonesia nab 30 in Pontianak hotel raid
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 11 — Indonesian authorities have detained 30 Malaysians suspected of running online scam activities from a hotel in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, allegedly targeting fellow Malaysians.
Pontianak Immigration Office chief Sam Fernando said the Malaysians, comprising 22 men and eight women, were detained along with a Taiwanese man at the hotel at about 11.15am on Tuesday in a joint operation with Pontianak City Police following intelligence on suspicious activities involving foreigners.
Sam said the 31 foreign nationals had used 14 rooms in the hotel for their activities.
“The targets were most likely Malaysian nationals. They were allegedly attempting to defraud Malaysian nationals,” he told a press conference on Thursday, according to a video uploaded online.
Based on the information obtained so far, Sam said there were no Indonesians among the targets.
All 31 were taken to the Pontianak Immigration Detention Centre for further questioning, with several items linked to the suspected activities also seized.
Sam said three Malaysian nationals were found to have overstayed, while there were also cases of misuse of stay permits for activities that were not in accordance with the purposes for which they were granted.
They also had not arrived together, with some entering through Pontianak airport, the Entikong land border crossing and Jakarta using various types of immigration permits, he said.
“The length of time they have been here varies. Some have been here for two months, while others for three weeks,” he said.
Sam said his office would coordinate with relevant Malaysian authorities as investigations into the case continued. — Bernama

Title: DNA results for five Long Lellang crash victims due by tomorrow, say Sarawak police
Article:
MIRI, Sept 11 — The deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) analysis for all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday is expected to be completed by tomorrow at the latest.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the remains would only be handed over to the respective next-of-kin once the DNA analysis was completed.
“We anticipate that the DNA analysis for the five victims could be completed by tomorrow at the latest,” he told reporters here today.
Earlier, post-mortem examinations on all five victims were completed at the hospital’s forensic department, with severe burn injuries identified as the cause of death.
Last Tuesday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama

Title: Newborn’s body found in Dungun hostel locker, police investigating
Article:
DUNGUN, Sept 11 — A 19-year-old student allegedly hid her newborn baby’s body in a hostel locker after giving birth in a toilet at an educational institution here two days ago.
Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the discovery of the body at 10.48pm yesterday.
He said the baby, believed to have been born at eight months’ gestation, was suspected to have died after birth.
Investigations found that the student allegedly wrapped the baby in cloth, placed the body in a bag, and kept it in a hostel locker.
“The matter came to light after the management of a mosque contacted the institution and informed them that the student had sought help to arrange the baby’s burial,” he said when contacted today.
Nik Ab Halim said police had recorded statements from several witnesses and examined the scene with assistance from the Forensic Unit.
The baby’s body was taken to Dungun Hospital for post-mortem and the case is being investigated under Section 318 of the Penal Code for concealment of birth. — Bernama

Title: Selangor sets Oct 26 as replacement holiday for Sultan’s Silver Jubilee
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 11 — Selangor has declared October 25 a special public holiday to commemorate the silver jubilee of Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah’s reign.
State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the holiday would be replaced on October 26 as the anniversary falls on a Sunday,
The Star
reported.
“Since the date falls on a Sunday, the following day, October 26 (Monday) is designated as the replacement public holiday,” he said during a press conference announcing details of the celebration.
He added that the holiday would be observed in the same way as the September 1 public holiday marking Selangor’s overall victory at Sukma 2026.
The September 1 holiday applied to all federal and state civil servants serving in Selangor, while private sector employers were encouraged to grant leave at their discretion.
Ahmad Fadzli said the jubilee celebration would feature around 20 programmes and official events, scheduled between September 28 and November 1.
The full list of events will be published on the social media platforms of the Selangor State Secretary’s Office.

Title: Was bad weather to blame? Investigators dig into what brought down deadly Long Lellang chopper
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau has begun its investigation into the cause of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang which claimed five lives, said Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah.
Hasbi said the ministry’s air accident investigation team was already at the crash site and was working to determine the cause of the tragedy.
“We will wait for the report from the Air Accident Investigation Team. We cannot say anything at this stage,” he said when met by reporters after launching the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme here on Friday.
Asked if bad weather could have caused the crash, Hasbi said it was too early to draw any conclusions.
“We will wait for the report. I cannot predict it because everything will depend on the investigation, including the weather,” he said, adding that the report was expected to be completed soon.
The BO-105 helicopter, registered 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing airport in Ulu Baram while conducting an FDS mission on Sept 8.
All five crew members, including the pilot, on board, were killed in the crash. They were identified as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — The Borneo Post

Title: Tanker driver, still hospitalised, charged with murder over Pahang crash that wiped out young family on Merdeka Day
Article:
TEMERLOH, Sept 11 — A cement tanker driver receiving treatment at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah was charged today with four counts of murder over a crash that killed four people on Aug 31.
No plea was recorded from the accused, Zulkarnain Md Noh, 52, after the charges were read before Magistrate Nuur Fakhizaa Abu Bakar, as the case falls under the High Court’s jurisdiction.
Zulkarnain is accused of having caused the deaths of Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef Muhammad Nazatullah and Seow Beng Wai.
The offences were allegedly committed at about 10.30pm on Aug 31 at KM110.3 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT) eastbound.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code (Act 574), which carries the death penalty, or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Najimi Arif Nasarudin and Anis Syakilla Zawawi appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
Magistrate Nuur Fakhizaa set Nov 12 for document submission and mention.
On Sept 1, four people were killed after a cement-laden tanker was believed to have lost control and crashed into several other vehicles that were moving slowly at the location.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob was reported to have said the three victims travelling in a Proton S70 were a married couple, Muhammad Nazatullah and Nur Atiqah Sofiya, and their son, while Seow Beng Wai was a passenger in a Honda CR-V.
He said Seow’s son, Sebastian Seow Jhen, 18, who was driving the Honda CR-V, and the tanker driver sustained serious injuries and were treated at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah in Temerloh.
The drivers and passengers of eight other vehicles, including an express bus, a Toyota Hilux, a Toyota Alphard and five other cars, suffered minor injuries. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar visits Kampung Numbak fire victims, pledges aid
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited and offered support to victims of the Kampung Numbak fire at the temporary relief centre at the Damai Multipurpose Hall here today.
Anwar, accompanied by Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, arrived at the relief centre at 1.30 pm and spent about 20 minutes meeting the victims.
The Prime Minister was then briefed on the fire by Kota Kinabalu Mayor Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah before handing over aid to the victims.
A total of 111 heads of household received food baskets as well as RM1,500 in special financial assistance from the federal government.
Earlier, Anwar and Hajiji joined more than 100 residents for Friday prayers at the nearby Masjid Jamek Kampung Likas.
One of the victims, Ruhin Nya Amrani, 52, said the assistance is a great help, particularly in covering the expenses of her two children, who are in secondary school.
“I am touched that the Prime Minister himself came to visit us and provide assistance. This will certainly help ease our burden,” she said.
Mohd Jamri Jamjiru, 43, said the government’s assistance will be put to good use.
“We appreciate all the assistance given, but what matters now is for the government to speed up efforts to rebuild our settlement,” he said.
The Kampung Numbak fire on Aug 30 destroyed about 200 houses built over the water, killing three people. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Umno proposing ‘Grand Collaboration’ to end political clashes in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — A proposal for the formation of a “Grand Collaboration” through political understanding (Tafahum Siyasi) among the country’s political party coalitions has been put forward to avoid political clashes that would be detrimental to the ummah and the nation, said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the concept does not involve a merger of political parties, but rather a common ground for mutual understanding aimed at preserving political stability and reinvigorating national economic growth.
He said the approach draws lessons from the wisdom of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah and the opening of Makkah, which demonstrated that political victory and understanding must be accompanied by the values of forgiveness, compassion and unity.
“This Grand Collaboration is not a merger of parties. Instead, it is an understanding aimed at avoiding clashes that would be detrimental. I understand and can sense the concerns of the Malays, who no longer want us to clash and quarrel among ourselves.
“However, in building this common ground, we are not forcing any party to dilute its identity. In other words, whoever Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) work with, Umno remains Umno, and Barisan Nasional remains Barisan Nasional,” he said.
He said this when delivering his presidential address at the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre (WTC) here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, outlined three key principles in guiding the Tafahum Siyasi understanding: prioritising common ground for the benefit of the ummah, respecting differences in ideology as well as the respective parties’ guidelines, and upholding the principle of flexibility in practising tolerance.
He also stressed that honesty and sincerity are key prerequisites that cannot be compromised in making the political understanding a success, in order to prevent a repeat of episodes of betrayal and broken agreements.
At the same time, Ahmad Zahid said Umno needs to remember its fundamental character as a party that does not merely think superficially from one election cycle to another, but is capable of planning the nation’s development with a long-term vision spanning generations.
According to Ahmad Zahid, the party’s struggle has always been underpinned by its ability to formulate inclusive socioeconomic plans for the well-being of the people and the nation.
He cited the introduction of the New Economic Policy (NEP) and the National Transformation 2050 (TN50) vision as examples of the party’s commitment to addressing the aspirations of new generations, including Gen Z and Gen Alpha.
“We need to remember Umno’s true character. We do not think only from one election term to the next. The reality is that Umno is a party that has always planned the nation’s development across generations.
“The NEP, for example, was not formulated to win applause for a season. TN50 was conceived to address the thinking and aspirations of Gen Z through to Gen Alpha. That is how a governing party thinks,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid said the party’s priority is not merely to win a series of elections, but to ensure that a strong national framework and direction can be passed on to the next generation of leaders. — Bernama

Title: Sabah gets RM1.5b MA63 boost, Anwar hints Sarawak could be next by Sept 16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The interim allocation for Sabah will immediately rise to RM1.5 billion this year, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said this in reply to a request from Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor during the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting (MTPMA63) press conference here.
Anwar pointed out the payment is an interim measure and that negotiations would continue, taking into account the country’s financial position, as provided for in the original agreement.
“However, if the increase is too small, it may be disputed. So, we will wait for Parliament in October to table the paper and then disburse the RM1.5 billion this year as well, perhaps at the end of October or early November,” he stated.
Hajiji had earlier, on behalf of the Sabah state government, also requested the settlement of the 40 per cent payment to Sabah.
“Therefore, we hope that this matter can also be resolved and expedited. That is on behalf of the Sabah government,” said Hajiji.
Separately, Anwar also said for Sarawak, although it is not included under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution, the same spirit should nevertheless be taken into consideration.
“Therefore, I will continue discussions with the Premier over the next few days. Hopefully, by 16th September, Malaysia Day in Kuching, I will also be able to announce an interim measure for Sarawak,” he said.
He added that Sarawak has also put forward its views on a formula that should be introduced, so that the formula clearly takes into account the country’s financial position and capacity, as well as the minimum that can be considered and the maximum.
“I agree and I have asked the Ministry of Finance and the Sarawak Ministry of Finance to discuss the introduction of such a formula,” said Anwar.
Sarawak Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg expressed his appreciation for the earlier discussion and for the decisions that have been reached. — The Borneo Post

Title: Perak orders caterer at Lenggong boarding school to shut after almost 160 students, staff fall sick
Article:
IPOH, September 11 — A food caterer serving a boarding school in Lenggong, Perak has been ordered to close after 159 students and staff developed symptoms of suspected food poisoning.
Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the Hulu Perak District Health Office received a report of the incident from Lenggong Health Clinic on September 10.
He said those affected, aged between 13 and 52, began developing symptoms from 11.30pm on September 9, with the latest case reported at 1.40pm the following day.
“Of the 159 cases, all experienced diarrhoea and abdominal pain, while 125 had headaches, 89 had nausea, 31 had vomiting and 15 had fever,” he said in a statement today.
All were treated by a medical team at the school, with 10 receiving further treatment at Lenggong Health Clinic, while none required hospitalisation and all remained stable.
Sivanesan said 34 clinical samples, 14 environmental samples and one food sample were collected and sent to the Ipoh Public Health Laboratory for analysis.
He said the suspected food was supplied for a programme at the school on September 9 by an external caterer engaged by the programme organiser.
The Hulu Perak District Health Office inspected the caterer’s premises at 2pm on September 10 and recorded a score of 78.16 per cent.
“Following the inspection, the food premises were ordered to close under Section 18(1)(d) of the Prevention and Control of Infectious Diseases Act 1988,” he said.
The operator was also ordered to clean the premises, carry out corrective measures and conduct regular pest control, while the school dining hall continued operating as usual.
Sivanesan also urged food handlers to comply with the Food Act 1983 and Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 to prevent further food poisoning incidents.

Title: Sounds like a ‘PM in waiting’, Khairy says of Zahid’s speech at Umno assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s keynote at the party’s general assembly this morning earned praise from Khairy Jamaluddin.
Khairy, an Umno returnee after being sacked three years ago for alleged disciplinary infractions and breaches of party discipline during GE15 – described the speech as crystal clear on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) direction ahead of the coming general election.
“This is the speech of a prime minister in waiting and a speech of a government in waiting,” Khairy told reporters after Zahid’s speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly here.
In his address, Zahid described Umno as a far-sighted party with a long-term vision for Malaysia, rather than one that merely hopes to survive one election after another.
He also called for the GE16 to be held as soon as possible, saying it was time for BN to seek a fresh mandate to lead the country.
Zahid further pledged that Malaysia’s courts and institutions would not be used as political tools should BN return to Putrajaya.
The third day of the assembly was also attended by four PAS leaders, including its vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad, secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, and assistant secretary-general Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman.

Title: No U-turn: Ex-minister Dr Zaliha says she has backed Health Service Commission proposal since 2023
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Former Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa today denied making a U-turn on the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission, saying she had remained committed to the initiative since 2023.
She said a report by a health portal yesterday, which claimed she had reversed her stance, was inaccurate and did not reflect the full context, stressing that efforts on the matter had continued throughout her tenure at the Ministry of Health (MOH).
In a statement, Dr Zaliha said that as early as February 2023, she had publicly stated that the proposal to establish the commission was among the key matters being considered in the final draft of the Health White Paper.
“In fact, in April 2023, the same news portal reported on my meeting with representatives of Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK), where the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission and a Health Reform Commission was discussed within the framework of the White Paper,” she said.
On her parliamentary reply on June 15, 2023, which she said had often been misinterpreted, Dr Zaliha explained that it was a clarification on the scope of authority of a Service Commission under Article 144 of the Federal Constitution.
She said the functions of a Service Commission cover appointments, confirmation of service, promotions, transfers and disciplinary action, but establishing such a commission does not give it the power to create new posts or formulate remuneration systems, including setting more competitive emolument rates.
“I also explained that establishing a new Service Commission would involve a complex process, including the need to amend the Federal Constitution and secure a two-thirds majority in both the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara.
“That explanation was about the structure, jurisdiction and limitations of the model available at the time, and was not an outright rejection of the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission,” she said.
Dr Zaliha cited records after the July 2023 parliamentary session showing that she had publicly confirmed the Government’s intention to establish the commission and was assessing the best model for it.
She said the commitment was followed by the establishment of a Technical Working Group by the MOH in October 2023 to identify the best methods and mechanisms for setting up the Health Service Commission.
Dr Zaliha reiterated that her position on the welfare of healthcare workers had remained unchanged, stressing that any reform of the healthcare service system, including the establishment of the commission, must be implemented urgently and backed by an authority capable of resolving the crises faced by healthcare personnel.
According to media reports yesterday, Dr Zaliha called for the Government to expedite the establishment of the commission following the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, but the news portal in question described the call as a “U-turn”. — Bernama

Title: DNA tests pending for five victims of Long Lellang helicopter crash, says Sarawak police
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 11 — The post-mortems on all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday were completed at 7.30pm yesterday.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the cause of death for all five victims was severe burn injuries sustained in the helicopter crash.
“For now, we are awaiting the results of the deoxyribonucleic acid samples for scientific confirmation,” he told Bernama.
On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, had crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama

Title: From complaint to compensation: How victims in Malaysia are winning sexual harassment cases
Article:
SEMPORNA, Sept 11 — The Sexual Harassment Tribunal Agency (Tags) under the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) recorded 134 sexual harassment complaints over a two-year period, with 90 of them successfully resolved.
Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the figures showed that Tags, which was established on March 8, 2024, played an important role as a main avenue for helping victims seek resolution and redress for the incidents they experienced.
“The figure only covers complaints received at KPWKM counters and does not include police reports. Male victims and children can also use this platform to seek redress. So far this year, four male victims have filed cases with the tribunal.
“Some victims have also won their cases and received compensation,” she told reporters after officiating the Semporna Zero Tolerance for Violence: Advocacy Against Sexual Harassment and End Violence Against Women programmes here yesterday.
She said KPWKM continued to provide support through advocacy, education and the provision of easily accessible assistance channels so that victims would not continue to remain silent when faced with sexual harassment.
Elaborating on the domestic violence statistics, Nancy said 4,646 cases had been reported nationwide up to July this year, including 424 cases in Sabah.
“The figures show that women’s safety requires more comprehensive, integrated and sustained action through a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach,” she said.
In addition, Nancy advised victims of violence or sexual harassment to have the courage to speak up through the proper channels and to keep evidence that could assist in the process of seeking redress. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: KPWKM are the Malay initials for the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development.

Title: Anwar: Time to make MA63 part of the national conversation, not just Sabah-Sarawak issue
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to become part of the national narrative rather than being viewed solely as an issue concerning Sabah and Sarawak.
He said the approach was important to ensure Malaysians understood that the government’s commitment to MA63 formed part of the Madani Government’s national policy and was closely linked to the country’s development, stability and unity.
Anwar said this must be understood and embraced by people in peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak as part of a national policy, commitment and narrative aimed at strengthening the country.
“I have proposed that discussions on MA63 be made part of the national narrative. It is very important because otherwise, it becomes a sectoral issue.
“Every year, we have to hold separate discussions on Sabah and Sarawak. No. This is a national commitment about development, stability, and what we promised when Malaysia was formed.
“This must be firmly established as a national narrative. We need to encourage Malaysians not to speak only about their race, party or group, but to engage in a broader discourse that strengthens the nation,” he told a press conference after chairing the 2026 Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
The Prime Minister said people in peninsular Malaysia should also not view additional allocations or measures implemented under MA63 as merely special considerations for Sabah and Sarawak.
Meanwhile, Abang Johari backed the proposal to place MA63 within a national framework, saying it would align provisions enshrined in the Federal Constitution with efforts to strengthen Malaysia’s unity.
“We want to align what is enshrined in the Constitution with the unity of Malaysia as a united nation, a united Malaysia, as we continue our efforts to develop the country,” he said.
He said the approach was more practical in balancing the interests of the Federal Government, Sabah and Sarawak, including in matters of finance and national development. — Bernama

Title: Sabah, Sarawak to get bigger share of Parliament seats, Anwar says as MA63 push moves ahead
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Sabah and Sarawak will get a higher proportion of parliamentary representation under a Cabinet decision in principle to increase the number of seats for the two Borneo states, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
Anwar said the Cabinet had agreed to increase the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak, although the exact number and mechanism had yet to be determined.
He stressed that any increase must also raise the proportion of seats held by the two states to reflect the spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
“An increase in the number of seats can be misleading. An increase does not necessarily mean that the ratio will improve; it could simply mean equalising the numbers.
“So the increase must be accompanied by an increase in the proportion of representation for Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a press conference after chairing the committee meeting for the implementation of the MA63 with Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg present.
Anwar added that there could also be an increase in seats for peninsular Malaysia.
He said the Cabinet made the decision last Wednesday and the Election Commission had been informed to begin discussions on the mechanism and number of additional seats.
Representatives from the two states would subsequently negotiate with political parties from peninsular Malaysia on the details, Anwar said.
Under the original Malaysia Agreement 1963, when Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak and Malaya formed the Federation, the three territories collectively held one-third of the parliamentary seats to prevent Malaya from unilaterally securing the two-thirds majority required to amend the Federal Constitution.
That proportion was reduced after Singapore left the federation in 1965. Of the 222 parliamentary seats today, Sabah has 25 and Sarawak 31, giving the two states a combined 25 per cent of the total compared with 75 per cent for peninsular Malaysia.
Sabah and Sarawak have been seeking a minimum one-third, or 33 per cent, share of parliamentary representation, which would require about 18 additional seats.
“So now we need to look at the mechanism. The principle is that there must be an increase that raises the proportion of representation. We have agreed to that. But the details and mechanics will be discussed with the Election Commission and the various states and political parties,” Anwar said.
Asked whether the increased representation could be implemented before the next general election, Anwar said he was uncertain whether there would be sufficient time.
“I am not certain whether there will be sufficient time because we have to follow the process. I do not want to interfere with the constitutional process. But the important thing is that the decision has been made and the Election Commission has been informed,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government was expediting the appointment of more Sabah- and Sarawak-born Malaysians to key government positions, another matter he said was recognised under MA63.
He said the first phase had already been implemented, while the second phase would be expedited.
Anwar described MA63 as a national commitment rather than an issue concerning only Sabah and Sarawak.
“I had proposed that discussions on MA63 be made part of the national narrative. This is very important because otherwise it becomes a sectoral matter that we have to discuss separately every year.
“It is a national commitment about development, stability, and the commitments we made at independence, Malaya in 1957 and Malaysia in 1963,” he said.
He said the issue should be viewed as part of efforts to strengthen Malaysia as a whole, rather than through the lens of race, political parties or regional interests.

Title: Zahid says Umno still hopes for favourable outcome after Najib clemency deferred
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today expressed disappointment over the postponement of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application, but said the party continues to hope for a favourable outcome.
Zahid said Umno respected the decision and would continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers while appealing to His Majesty the King to use his wisdom in deciding Najib’s application.
“We are saddened by the decision. Nevertheless, we continue to express our deepest respect to His Majesty the King, and we appeal to His Majesty to use all his wisdom to make the best decision.
“We continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers. We continue to support the Rulers, and we hope that something favourable will be granted to Datuk Seri Najib Abdul Razak,” he told reporters after delivering his policy speech at Umno’s general assembly here.
The Prime Minister’s Department today said Najib’s clemency application had been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board.
The department – which covers Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya – said the board held its 63rd meeting this morning with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consenting to the postponement.
Earlier this morning Zahid expressed hope for the “best” news for Najib during his policy speech at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
Umno delegates greeted Najib’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, enthusiastically with applause after Zahid asked her to stand for a moment during his speech.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison and a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on August 23, 2022.
In 2024, the Federal Territories Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
Najib and his lawyers subsequently argued that the partial pardon included a royal addendum allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, and sued to have it enforced.
On December  22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest.
Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.
